[[File:Flat plate 10.gif|border|thumb|Particle simulation of Argon gas flowing over a flat plate at angle of attack]]
'''Rarefied gas dynamics''' is a branch of [[fluid mechanics]] where the [[continuum assumption]] is no longer accurate, as a characteristic [[length scale]] in the  [[gas]]  (e.g. radius of a body moving in a gas, radius of a tube conducting a gas, etc.) becomes comparable to the [[mean free path]] of gaseous particles. Consequently, the gas cannot be described as a [[Continuum assumption|continuum]]. Instead, the gas should be described by its microstate determined by the velocity and position of each particle. Since it would be an impossible computational task in storing the very large volumes of information involved in tracking the behavior of every single particle, the statistical or [[kinetic theory of gases]]<ref name="cercignani">
{{Cite book |last=Cercignani |first=Carlo |title=Rarefied Gas Dynamics: From Basic Concepts to Actual Calculations |date=2000-02-28 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-65992-5 |language=en |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=klvag3ULC6QC&dq=cercignani+rarefied+gas+dynamics+ISBN&pg=PR11}}
</ref><ref name="roohi">
{{Cite book |last1=Roohi |last2=Akhlaghi |last3=Stefanov |first3=Stefan |title=Advances in Direct Simulation Monte Carlo: From Micro-Scale to Rarefied Flow Phenomena |date=2025 |publisher=Springer Singapore |location=Singapore |doi=10.1007/978-981-96-8200-3 |isbn=978-981-96-8199-0}}
</ref> must be used. This theory consists in obtaining the macroscopic state of the gas described by quantities such as density, bulk velocity, temperature, pressure tensor, and heat flux from the microstate of the gas. To describe non-equilibrium phenomena in rarefied gases, the [[Boltzmann equation|Boltzmann transport equation]] must be used, which is the appropriate mathematical tool for this purpose.<ref name=":02">

== Brief history ==
The history of rarefied gas dynamics starts with the [[kinetic theory of gases]]. In 1860, [[James Clerk Maxwell|Maxwell]] published results on the distribution of molecular velocities for a [[gas]] in equilibrium, which is called the [[Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution|Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Maxwell |first1=J. C. |title=II. ''Illustrations of the dynamical theory of gases'' |journal=The London, Edinburgh, and Dublin Philosophical Magazine and Journal of Science |date=1860 |volume=20 |issue=130 |pages=21–37 |doi=10.1080/14786446008642902 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Clerk Maxwell |first=James |date=1867 |title=On the Dynamical Theory of Gases |journal= Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London |series=Series I|volume=157 |pages=49–88 |bibcode=1867RSPT..157...49C }}</ref> As a result, the assumption that all molecules move with the same speed was abandoned and the random nature of molecular motion was recognized. In 1872, [[Ludwig Boltzmann|Boltzmann]] derived an integro-differential equation ([[Boltzmann equation]]) to describe the evolution of the [[Distribution function (measure theory)|velocity distribution function]] in space and time.<ref name="Ferziger1972">{{Cite book |last1=Ferziger |first1=Joel H. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=mxS2AAAAIAAJ&q=Mathematical+theory+of+transport+processes+in+gases-NH |title=Mathematical Theory of Transport Processes in Gases |last2=Kaper |first2=H. G. |date=1972 |publisher=North-Holland Publishing Company |isbn=978-0-7204-2046-3 |language=en}}</ref><ref>Boltzmann, Ludwig. "Further studies on the thermal equilibrium of gas molecules." ''The kinetic theory of gases: an anthology of classic papers with historical commentary''. 2003. 262-349.</ref>  In the same paper, Boltzmann proved the [[H-theorem]] demonstrating that intermolecular collisions always produce [[entropy]]. In other words, the [[Boltzmann equation]] is [[Irreversible process|irreversible]].

In 1912, Hilbert proved the existence and uniqueness of a solution of the [[Boltzmann equation|Boltzmann Equation]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Hilbert |first=D. |title=Grundzüge einer Allgemeinen Theorie der linearen Integralgleichungen |publisher=Chelsea Publishing Co. |year=1953 |isbn=978-1-4297-0236-2}}</ref> A connection between the kinetic theory and fluid dynamics was done by [[Chapman–Enskog theory|Chapman and Enskog]]<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1916 |title=VI. On the law of distribution of molecular velocities, and on the theory of viscosity and thermal conduction, in a non-uniform simple monatomic gas |journal= Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London, Series A |language=en |volume=216 |issue=538–548 |pages=279–348 |doi=10.1098/rsta.1916.0006 |bibcode=1916RSPTA.216..279C |issn=0264-3952 |last1=Chapman |first1=S. |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |date=1918 |title=V. On the kinetic theory of a gas. Part II.—A composite monatomic gas: diffusion, viscosity, and thermal conduction |journal= Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society of London, Series A |language=en |volume=217 |issue=549–560 |pages=115–197 |doi=10.1098/rsta.1918.0005 |bibcode=1918RSPTA.217..115C |issn=0264-3952 |last1=Chapman |first1=S. |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref name="Ferziger1972" />  who derived the Euler and Navier-Stokes equations based upon a series expansion of the [[Boltzmann equation]] with respect to the [[Knudsen number]]. This approach allowed to derive expressions for the [[viscosity]] and [[thermal conductivity]] directly from [[Interatomic potential|intermolecular interaction potentials]].  Furthermore, considering higher order terms of the expansion, Burnett derived more general constitutive equations for the pressure tensor and heat flux.<ref>{{Cite journal | last=Burnett |first=D.|title=The distribution of molecular velocities and the mean motion in non-uniform gas  |journal=Proc. London Math. Soc. |date=1935 |volume=40|pages=382–435}}</ref> Then, Grad proved the equivalence of the equations of [[fluid dynamics]] to an asymptotic form of the Boltzmann equation.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Grad |first=Harold |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qSN4sMWEB-IC&dq=Grad+1965+asymptotic+equivalence+of+the+navier+stokes&pg=PA4 |title=Asymptotic Equivalence of the Navier-Stokes and Nonlinear Boltzmann Equations |date=1964 |publisher=Magneto-Fluid Dynamics Division, Courant Institute of Mathematical Sciences, New York University |language=en}}</ref>  The scientific branch of rarefied gas dynamics consolidated in the 19th century and became forefront with space exploration. As a result, the first international symposium on rarefied gas dynamics was held in Nice, France in July 1958.<ref name=":02"/>

== Knudsen number ==
To determine if a [[gas]] can be classified as ''rarefied'', the non-dimensional [[Knudsen number|Knudsen]] number is usually calculated. The [[Knudsen number|Knudsen]] number <chem>\mathrm{Kn}</chem> is defined as the ratio of  the  [[Mean free path|mean free path <math>\lambda</math>]],  to a characteristic [[length scale]] <math>L</math> in the flow,<ref name=":4" /> i.e. <chem>\mathrm{Kn}</chem>=<math>\lambda/L</math>. The value of the [[Knudsen number|Knudsen]] number tells you whether a  molecular modeling approach must be used or a [[Macroscopic scale|macroscopic]] description is sufficient.  High and intermediate Knudsen numbers mean that the gas is rarefied, while very small [[Knudsen number|Knudsen]] numbers imply that the gas is a continuum. Various flow regimes can be distinguished based on the value of the [[Knudsen number|Knudsen]] number. Namely, a gas flow regime can be characterized as continuum (or viscous), slip, transitional, and [[Free molecular flow|free-molecular]].<ref name=":12" /><ref name=":17">{{Cite journal |last1=Sun |first1=Quanhua |last2=Boyd |first2=Iain D. |date=March 25, 2002 |title=A Direct Simulation Method for Subsonic, Microscale Gas Flows |journal=Journal of Computational Physics |volume=179 |issue=2 |pages=400–425 |doi=10.1006/jcph.2002.7061 |bibcode=2002JCoPh.179..400S |issn=0021-9991}}</ref>

The following rough ranges of the Knudsen number for these regimes are usually established: 
* <chem>\mathrm{Kn}</chem><math> < 0.01</math> for continuum or viscous regime; 
* <math>0.01 < </math><chem>\mathrm{Kn}</chem><math> < 0.10</math>  for slip flow regime;             
* <math>0.1 < </math> <chem>\mathrm{Kn}</chem> <math>< 10</math>   for transitional regime;
* <chem>\mathrm{Kn}</chem> <math>> 10</math> for [[Free molecular flow|free-molecular]] regime.

This division between the regimes can vary depending on flow type and required accuracy. The mathematical approach and tool to model a gas flow depends on the flow regime. In the continuum regime, the gas is not ''rarefied'' and hence can be described by the [[Euler equations (fluid dynamics)|Euler]] or [[Navier–Stokes equations|Navier-Stokes]] equations. In the slip flow regime, the [[Navier–Stokes equations|Navier-Stokes]] equations are applied too, but the velocity no-slip and temperature continuity boundary conditions are replaced by the velocity slip and temperature jump conditions.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last1=Lofthouse |first1=Andrew J. |last2=Scalabrin |first2=Leonardo C. |last3=Boyd |first3=Iain D. |title=Velocity Slip and Temperature Jump in Hypersonic Aerothermodynamics |journal=Journal of Thermophysics and Heat Transfer |date=2008 |volume=22 |pages=38–49 |doi=10.2514/1.31280 |hdl=2027.42/76244 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref  name="Sharipov slip" >{{cite journal |last= Sharipov |first=Felix |date=2011|title= Data on the velocity slip and temperature jump on a gas-solid interface |journal=  J. Phys. Chem. Ref. Data  |volume=40 |issue=2 |article-number=023101 |doi=10.1063/1.3580290|bibcode=2011JPCRD..40b3101S }}</ref> All approaches to model gas flows in the transitional regime are based on the [[Boltzmann equation|Boltzmann transport equation]]. Since the intermolecular collisions are neglected in the free-molecular regime, the Boltzmann equation is applied in its simplified form.

== Velocity distribution function==

When the [[Continuum assumption|continuum]] assumption is fulfilled, the [[Molecule|molecular]] nature of the [[gas]] is neglected and the spatial and temporal variations of the flow are described in terms of its macroscopic properties such as [[velocity]], [[density]], [[pressure]], and [[temperature]].  In this case, the [[Navier–Stokes equations|Navier-Stokes]] equations provides the appropriate mathematical model of fluid flows. However, the [[Continuum assumption|continuum]] assumption is broken in a rarefied gas flow, therefore a modeling of such a flow is based on the [[Boltzmann equation|Boltzmann transport equation]].<ref name=":4" /><ref name=":6"/> In this case, the molecular nature of the [[gas]] must be considered <ref>{{Cite journal |last=Muntz |first=E. |date=1989-01-01 |title=Rarefied Gas Dynamics |journal=Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics |volume=21 |issue=1 |pages=387–417 |doi=10.1146/annurev.fluid.21.1.387 |issn=0066-4189}}</ref>  by means of the velocity distribution function <math>f(t,\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})</math>  where <math>t</math> is the time, <math>\mathbf{r}</math> is a vector of spatial coordinates and <math>\mathbf{v}</math> is a velocity of molecules.  This function provides a statistical description of the gas on the  molecular level.<ref name=":4" /> Taking [[Moment (mathematics)|moments]] of the velocity distribution function leads to macroscopic properties of a gas flow, thus providing the connection between microscopic and macroscopic levels.  The evolution of the [[Distribution function (measure theory)|velocity distribution function]] is described by the [[Boltzmann equation]],  which is valid for a dilute gas. In such a gas, the mean distance between molecules is significantly larger than the molecular size, meaning that the intermolecular collisions are predominantly binary.<ref name=":12">{{cite book |last1=Boyd |first1=Iain D. |last2=Schwartzentruber |first2=Thomas E. |title=Nonequilibrium Gas Dynamics and Molecular Simulation |date=2017 |doi=10.1017/9781139683494 |isbn=978-1-107-07344-9 }}{{page needed|date=January 2026}}</ref> Another important assumption<ref name="cercignani" /> in the derivation of the [[Boltzmann equation|Boltzmann transport equation]]  is [[molecular chaos]], which means that the velocities of particles during their free motion between collisions are uncorrelated, and independent of their positions.

When a rarefied gas is restricted by a solid surface, the interaction of the gas molecules with this surfaces should be considered.<ref name=":02"/> Such an interaction leads to the momentum and heat transfer between the gas and the solid surface. This implies that the [[Boltzmann equation]] must be accompanied by boundary conditions determined by the interaction of gas molecules with the solid walls.<ref name="cercignani" />

== Mathematical approaches ==

The [[Boltzmann equation]] is valid for a dilute gas flow in the whole range of the [[Knudsen number]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cercignani |first=Carlo |date=1988 |title=The Boltzmann Equation and Its Applications |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-1-4612-1039-9?error=cookies_not_supported&code=51b5a2dd-fda0-4660-bc9b-a682e4f698f9 |journal=Applied Mathematical Sciences |doi=10.1007/978-1-4612-1039-9 |issn=0066-5452|url-access=subscription }}</ref> However, a general solution of this equation requires significant computational effort, therefore several mathematical approaches to model rarefied gases were developed depending on the flow regime.

===Slip flow regime===

In the slip flow regime, the gas rarefaction is moderate allowing to use a Navier-Stokes solver subject to the velocity slip and temperature jump boundary conditions on a solid surface.<ref name="Sharipov slip"/><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Aoki |first1=Kazuo |last2=Baranger |first2=Céline |last3=Hattori |first3=Masanari |last4=Kosuge |first4=Shingo |last5=Martalò |first5=Giorgio |last6=Mathiaud |first6=Julien |last7=Mieussens |first7=Luc |title=Slip Boundary Conditions for the Compressible Navier–Stokes Equations |journal=Journal of Statistical Physics |date=2017 |volume=169 |issue=4 |pages=744–781 |doi=10.1007/s10955-017-1886-8 |bibcode=2017JSP...169..744A |url=https://hal.science/hal-01634602 }}</ref> The slip and jump coefficients calculated on the molecular level are universal and can be applied to any geometrical configuration of the gas flow.

===Free molecular regime===

In the free molecular regime, the intermolecular collisions are neglected so that each particle moves independently on each other. In this case, the Boltzmann equation is significantly simplified. All macroscopic properties of a gas flow around a convex body are obtained in the form of integral, since a gas molecule undergoes only one interaction with the body surface. Internal flows and external flows around a concave body involve multiple gas-surface interactions. In this case, the  macroscopic characteristics are calculated from an integral equation. An alternative approach is the test particle [[Monte Carlo method]] consisting in tracking of a large number of model particles. Since the intermolecular collisions are neglected, the molecular trajectories are independent of each other and can be modeled serially. All these approaches are described in detail in the book by Bird.<ref name=":4"/>

===Transitional regime===

The transitional regime is hardest for mathematical modeling, because the continuum assumption is broken and the intermolecular collisions cannot be neglected. Therefore, the [[Boltzmann equation]] should be solved for any specific gas flow. The discrete velocity method and fast spectral method are typically used for this task. However, an application of this method to the Boltzmann equation in its exact form is very costly so that, till now, only few very simple problems have been solved by this way.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Sharipov |first1=Felix |last2=Bertoldo |first2=Guilherme |title=Poiseuille flow and thermal creep based on the Boltzmann equation with the Lennard-Jones potential over a wide range of the Knudsen number |journal=Physics of Fluids |date=2009 |volume=21 |issue=6 |article-number=067101 |doi=10.1063/1.3156011 |bibcode=2009PhFl...21f7101S }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dodulad |first1=O. I. |last2=Tcheremissine |first2=F. G. |title=Computation of a shock wave structure in monatomic gas with accuracy control |journal=Computational Mathematics and Mathematical Physics |date=2013 |volume=53 |issue=6 |pages=827–844 |doi=10.1134/S0965542513060055 |bibcode=2013CMMPh..53..827D }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jaiswal |first1=Shashank |last2=Alexeenko |first2=Alina A. |last3=Hu |first3=Jingwei |title=A discontinuous Galerkin fast spectral method for the full Boltzmann equation with general collision kernels |journal=Journal of Computational Physics |date=2019 |volume=378 |pages=178–208 |doi=10.1016/j.jcp.2018.11.001 |arxiv=1809.10186 |bibcode=2019JCoPh.378..178J }}</ref> To reduce the computational cost, the Boltzmann equation is replaced by its simplified form called a model kinetic equation. Three commonly used model equations are Bhatnagar, Gross, Krook (BGK),<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bhatnagar |first1=P. L. |last2=Gross |first2=E. P. |last3=Krook |first3=M. |title=A Model for Collision Processes in Gases. I. Small Amplitude Processes in Charged and Neutral One-Component Systems |journal=Physical Review |date=1954 |volume=94 |issue=3 |pages=511–525 |doi=10.1103/PhysRev.94.511 |bibcode=1954PhRv...94..511B }}</ref> Ellipsoidal Statistical (ES-model),<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Holway |first1=Lowell H. |title=New Statistical Models for Kinetic Theory: Methods of Construction |journal=The Physics of Fluids |date=1966 |volume=9 |issue=9 |pages=1658–1673 |doi=10.1063/1.1761920 |bibcode=1966PhFl....9.1658H }}</ref> and Shakhov (S-model).<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Shakhov |first1=E. M. |title=Generalization of the Krook kinetic relaxation equation |journal=Fluid Dynamics |date=1972 |volume=3 |issue=5 |pages=95–96 |doi=10.1007/BF01029546 }}</ref>  The computational effort to solve these model equations is essentially smaller than that to solve the Boltzmann equation itself and, at the same time, they are appropriate to solve practical problems with a reasonable accuracy. Some examples of numerical solvers are based on the model equations can be found here.<ref name=":6" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Xu |first1=Kun |last2=Huang |first2=Juan-Chen |title=A unified gas-kinetic scheme for continuum and rarefied flows |journal=Journal of Computational Physics |date=2010 |volume=229 |issue=20 |pages=7747–7764 |doi=10.1016/j.jcp.2010.06.032 |bibcode=2010JCoPh.229.7747X }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tumuklu |first1=Ozgur |last2=Li |first2=Zheng |last3=Levin |first3=Deborah A. |title=Particle Ellipsoidal Statistical Bhatnagar–Gross–Krook Approach for Simulation of Hypersonic Shocks |journal=AIAA Journal |date=2016 |volume=54 |issue=12 |pages=3701–3716 |doi=10.2514/1.J054837 |bibcode=2016AIAAJ..54.3701T }}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Alexeenko |first1=Alina |last2=Galitzine |first2=Cyril |last3=Alekseenko |first3=Alexander |title=40th Thermophysics Conference |chapter=High-Order Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Boltzmann Model Equations |date=2008 |doi=10.2514/6.2008-4256 |isbn=978-1-60086-991-4 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal
 |last1=Guo |first1=Zhaoli
 |last2=Xu |first2=Kun
 |last3=Wang |first3=Ruijie
 |title=Discrete unified gas kinetic scheme for all Knudsen number flows: Low-speed isothermal case
 |journal=Physical Review E
 |year=2013
 |volume=88
 |issue=3
 |article-number=033305
 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.88.033305
}}</ref>

The [[Direct simulation Monte Carlo|Direct Simulation Monte Carlo]] (DSMC) is a probabilistic method proposed by G.A. Bird.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite book |last=Bird |first=G. A. |title=The DSMC method |date=2013 |publisher=G. A. Bird |isbn=978-1-4921-1290-7 |edition=Version 1.2 |location=S.l.}}</ref> It consists of tracking of a huge number of model particles simultaneously decoupling the processes of their free motion and collisions between them. After alternating these two processes many times, the macroscopic characteristics are calculated based on the information about positions and velocities of the model particles. A result obtained by a valid implementation of the DSMC method is equivalent to that obtained from the [[Boltzmann equation]]. The DSMC method is easily applied to complicated geometrical configurations and to flows with chemical reactions and is a widely used method to solve scientific and engineering problems related to highly non-equilibrium gas flows.<ref name=":12" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Alexander |first1=Francis J. |last2=Garcia |first2=Alejandro L. |title=The Direct Simulation Monte Carlo Method |journal=Computers in Physics |date=1997 |volume=11 |issue=6 |pages=588–593 |doi=10.1063/1.168619 |bibcode=1997ComPh..11..588A }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Schwartzentruber |first1=Thomas E. |last2=Grover |first2=Maninder S. |last3=Valentini |first3=Paolo |date=October 2018 |title=Direct Molecular Simulation of Nonequilibrium Dilute Gases |journal=Journal of Thermophysics and Heat Transfer |volume=32 |issue=4 |pages=892–903 |doi=10.2514/1.t5188 }}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=DSMC 2023 Conference |url=https://www.sandia.gov/dsmc/ |access-date=2024-06-18 |website=Direct Simulation Monte Carlo DSMC |language=en-US}}</ref> It has also been applied to simulate ultra-cold quantum gases.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Wade |first1=A. C. J. |last2=Baillie |first2=D. |last3=Blakie |first3=P. B. |title=Direct simulation Monte Carlo method for cold-atom dynamics: Classical Boltzmann equation in the quantum collision regime |journal=Physical Review A |date=2011 |volume=84 |issue=2 |article-number=023612 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.84.023612 |arxiv=1105.2340 |bibcode=2011PhRvA..84b3612W }}</ref> For weakly non-equilibrium flows,  the discrete velocity method applied to the Boltzmann equation or to its model is more efficient than the DSMC method.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Clarke |first1=Peter |last2=Varghese |first2=Philip |last3=Goldstein |first3=David |title=A low noise discrete velocity method for the Boltzmann equation with quantized rotational and vibrational energy |journal=Journal of Computational Physics |date=2018 |volume=352 |pages=326–340 |doi=10.1016/j.jcp.2017.08.065 |bibcode=2018JCoPh.352..326C }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Oblapenko |first1=Georgii |last2=Goldstein |first2=David |last3=Varghese |first3=Philip |last4=Moore |first4=Christopher |title=Velocity-Space Hybridization of Direct Simulation Monte Carlo and a Quasi-Particle Boltzmann Solver |journal=Journal of Thermophysics and Heat Transfer |date=2021 |volume=35 |issue=4 |pages=788–799 |doi=10.2514/1.T6074 |osti=1765750 }}</ref>

More recent multiscale kinetic approaches seek to bridge the continuum, transitional, and free-molecular regimes within a single formulation. One example is the unified gas-kinetic framework, which classifies molecules according to their collision histories over an observation time scale and recovers the Boltzmann and Navier–Stokes descriptions as limiting cases.<ref>{{cite journal
 |last1=Guo |first1=Zhaoli
 |last2=Xu |first2=Kun
 |last3=Zhu |first3=Yajun
 |title=A unified gas-kinetic framework from Boltzmann to Navier–Stokes scales
 |journal=Advances in Aerodynamics
 |year=2026
 |volume=8
 |article-number=5
 |doi=10.1186/s42774-025-00252-1
 |doi-access=free
|arxiv=2508.07189
 }}</ref>

== Applications ==
=== High altitude flight and hypersonic flows ===

Applications of rarefied gas dynamic methods include [[hypersonic flight]] and [[atmospheric entry]], such as satellites in orbit, spacecraft or rockets re-entering Earth atmosphere, or entering atmosphere of another planet, or [[Hypersonic Cruise Vehicle|hypersonic cruise vehicles]]. These application areas often need RGD methods.<ref name=":11">{{cite book |last1=Nagnibeda |first1=E. A. |last2=Kustova |first2=E. V. |title=Non-Equilibrium Reacting Gas Flows |series=Heat and Mass Transfer |date=2009 |publisher=Springer-Verlag Berlin |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-01390-4 |isbn=978-3-642-01389-8 }}{{page needed|date=January 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Ivanov |first1=M. S. |last2=Gimelshein |first2=S. F. |title=Computational Hypersonic Rarefied Flows |journal=Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics |date=1998 |volume=30 |pages=469–505 |doi=10.1146/annurev.fluid.30.1.469 |bibcode=1998AnRFM..30..469I }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Theofilis |first1=Vassilis |last2=Pirozzoli |first2=Sergio |last3=Martin |first3=Pino |title=Special issue on the fluid mechanics of hypersonic flight |journal=Theoretical and Computational Fluid Dynamics |date=2022 |volume=36 |issue=1 |pages=1–8 |doi=10.1007/s00162-022-00605-2 |bibcode=2022ThCFD..36....1T |hdl=11573/1629119 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite journal |last1=Sharipov |first1=Felix |title=Hypersonic flow of rarefied gas near the Brazilian satellite during its reentry into atmosphere |journal=Brazilian Journal of Physics |date=2003 |volume=33 |issue=2 |pages=398–405 |doi=10.1590/S0103-97332003000200044 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2003BrJPh..33..398S }}</ref> In addition, even within a mostly [[continuum assumption|continuum]] flow around a high-speed vehicle, there may be local regions of rarefied flow as in the wake of the vehicle or near sharp-leading edges. These rarefied flow regions must be modelled appropriately in order to determine, e.g., the drag and heating to the vehicle and the radiation emitted and plasma blackout. It also includes understanding the damage impact of micrometer aerosol atmospheric particles on the material [[Ablation|erosion]] and heating at the surface.<ref name=":10">{{cite journal |last1=Habeck |first1=Joseph B. |last2=Kroells |first2=Michael D. |last3=Schwartzentruber |first3=Thomas E. |last4=Candler |first4=Graham V. |title=Characterization of Particle-Surface Impacts on a Sphere-Cone at Hypersonic Flight Conditions |journal=AIAA Journal |date=2024 |volume=62 |issue=2 |pages=460–475 |doi=10.2514/1.J062945 |bibcode=2024AIAAJ..62..460H }}</ref>

=== Plumes and jets ===

An example of rarefied gas dynamics that combines both low density and small length scales involve [[Thrusters (spacecraft)|thrusters]] on spacecraft used for maneuvering in outer space as well as [[Plume (fluid dynamics)|rocket plumes]] impinging on surfaces.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cai |first1=Chunpei |title=Rocket Plume Modeling |journal=AIAA Journal |date=2014 |volume=52 |issue=12 |pages=2907–2910 |doi=10.2514/1.J053351 |bibcode=2014AIAAJ..52.2907C }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Karpuzcu |first1=Irmak T. |last2=Levin |first2=Deborah A. |title=Study of Side-Jet Interactions over a Hypersonic Cone Flow Using Kinetic Methods |journal=AIAA Journal |date=2023 |volume=61 |issue=11 |pages=4741–4751 |doi=10.2514/1.J063020 |bibcode=2023AIAAJ..61.4741K }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Morris |first1=Aaron B. |last2=Goldstein |first2=David B. |last3=Varghese |first3=Philip L. |last4=Trafton |first4=Laurence M. |title=Approach for Modeling Rocket Plume Impingement and Dust Dispersal on the Moon |journal=Journal of Spacecraft and Rockets |date=2015 |volume=52 |issue=2 |pages=362–374 |doi=10.2514/1.A33058 |bibcode=2015JSpRo..52..362M }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gimelshein |first1=Natalia E. |last2=Lyons |first2=Robert B. |last3=Reuster |first3=James G. |last4=Gimelshein |first4=Sergey F. |title=Analysis of Ultraviolet Radiation Predictions from High Altitude Two-Phase Plumes |journal=AIAA Journal |date=2009 |volume=47 |issue=10 |pages=2486–2492 |doi=10.2514/1.44067 |bibcode=2009AIAAJ..47.2486G }}</ref>

=== Flow inside material microstructure ===
Rarefied gas dynamic methods are used for modeling gas flow around porous carbon-fiber materials at the microscale when designing [[Thermal protection system|heat shields]] for spacecraft<ref name=":8">{{Cite journal |last1=Kroells |first1=Michael |last2=Ramjatan |first2=Sahadeo |last3=Schwartzentruber |first3=Thomas E. |title=Aerothermal Loads on a Representative Porous Mesostructure at Flight Conditions Using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo |journal=Journal of Thermophysics and Heat Transfer |date=2024 |volume=38 |issue=4 |pages=491–507 |doi=10.2514/1.T6894 }}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite journal |last1=Fu |first1=Rui |last2=Martin |first2=Alexandre |last3=Ramjatan |first3=Sahadeo |last4=Kroells |first4=Michael |last5=Schwartzentruber |first5=Thomas E. |title=Microscale Thermal–Structural Modeling for Carbon Fibers Subjected to a Hypersonic Boundary Layer |journal=Journal of Spacecraft and Rockets |date=2025 |volume=62 |issue=1 |pages=7–17 |doi=10.2514/1.A35916 |bibcode=2025JSpRo..62....7F }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jambunathan |first1=Revathi |last2=Levin |first2=Deborah A. |last3=Borner |first3=Arnaud |last4=Ferguson |first4=Joseph C. |last5=Panerai |first5=Francesco |title=Prediction of gas transport properties through fibrous carbon preform microstructures using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo |journal=International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer |date=2019 |volume=130 |pages=923–937 |doi=10.1016/j.ijheatmasstransfer.2018.11.006 |bibcode=2019IJHMT.130..923J }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Poovathingal |first1=Savio |last2=Stern |first2=Eric C. |last3=Nompelis |first3=Ioannis |last4=Schwartzentruber |first4=Thomas E. |last5=Candler |first5=Graham V. |title=Nonequilibrium flow through porous thermal protection materials, Part II: Oxidation and pyrolysis |journal=Journal of Computational Physics |date=2019 |volume=380 |pages=427–441 |doi=10.1016/j.jcp.2018.02.043 |bibcode=2019JCoPh.380..427P }}</ref> with the objective of characterizing the aerothermal loading (e.g. heat flux, shear stress) and concentrations of atomic species inside the material microstructure. Here the mean free path approaches the length scale of the carbon-fibers of <math>10  \mu m </math>.

=== MEMS and NEMS ===
Very small length scales can also result in rarefied gas phenomena. [[MEMS|Micro-Electro-Mechanical systems]] (MEMS) and [[Nanoelectromechanical systems]] (NEMS), which involve the fabrication and operation of microscopic devices,  involve the motion of gases at very small length scales including <math>1  \mu m </math> or <math>10^{-6}</math> m resulting in rarefied gas dynamics<ref>{{cite book |last1=Aluru |first1=Narayan R. |last2=Karniadakis |first2=George Em |title=Micro/Nano Technology Systems for Biomedical Applications |chapter=Numerical Simulation of Microflows and Nanoflows |date=2010 |pages=53–120 |doi=10.1093/acprof:oso/9780199219698.003.0003 |isbn=978-0-19-921969-8 }}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Li |first1=Jun |title=Multiscale and Multiphysics Flow Simulations of Using the Boltzmann Equation |chapter=Simulation Methods for Rarefied Gas Flows |date=2020 |pages=67–117 |doi=10.1007/978-3-030-26466-6_3 |isbn=978-3-030-26465-9 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Patronis |first1=Alexander |last2=Lockerby |first2=Duncan A. |last3=Borg |first3=Matthew K. |last4=Reese |first4=Jason M. |date=2013-12-15 |title=Hybrid continuum–molecular modelling of multiscale internal gas flows |journal=Journal of Computational Physics |volume=255 |pages=558–571 |doi=10.1016/j.jcp.2013.08.033 |bibcode=2013JCoPh.255..558P |issn=0021-9991|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Varoutis |first1=S. |last2=Valougeorgis |first2=D. |last3=Sharipov |first3=F. |title=Simulation of gas flow through tubes of finite length over the whole range of rarefaction for various pressure drop ratios |journal=Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology A: Vacuum, Surfaces, and Films |date=2009 |volume=27 |issue=6 |pages=1377–1391 |doi=10.1116/1.3248273 |bibcode=2009JVSTA..27.1377V }}</ref>

=== Gas flows around particulates and droplets ===

Solid or liquid particulates or droplets suspended in a gas flow often have size scales of <math>1  \mu m </math> or less, leading to Kn near the particle of the order 1 and the need to include rarefaction effects. Computation of important quantities such as particle drag or heat transfer between the particle and the gas may need to use rarefied gas dynamic methods.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Clercx |first1=H.J.H. |last2=Livi |first2=C. |last3=Di Staso |first3=G. |last4=Toschi |first4=F. |title=Modeling drag coefficients of spheroidal particles in rarefied flow conditions |journal=European Journal of Mechanics - B/Fluids |date=2024 |volume=108 |pages=90–103 |doi=10.1016/j.euromechflu.2024.07.008 |bibcode=2024EuJMB.108...90C }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Cheremisin |first1=A.A. |last2=Kushnarenko |first2=A.V. |title=Photophoretic interaction of aerosol particles and its effect on coagulation in rarefied gas medium |journal=Journal of Aerosol Science |date=2013 |volume=62 |pages=26–39 |doi=10.1016/j.jaerosci.2013.03.011 |bibcode=2013JAerS..62...26C }}</ref><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Filippov |first1=A.V. |last2=Rosner |first2=D.E. |title=Energy transfer between an aerosol particle and gas at high temperature ratios in the Knudsen transition regime |journal=International Journal of Heat and Mass Transfer |date=2000 |volume=43 |issue=1 |pages=127–138 |doi=10.1016/S0017-9310(99)00113-1 |bibcode=2000IJHMT..43..127F |doi-access=free }}</ref>

=== Radiometric phenomena ===

A variety of interesting phenomena and micro-device concepts have been investigated that rely on the effects of temperature differences acting in the rarefied or transitional gas-flow regime.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Alexeenko |first1=Alina A. |last2=Strongrich |first2=A. S. |last7=Shivkumar |first7=G. |title=Microdevices enabled by rarefied flow phenomena |journal=AIP Conference Proceedings |date=2016 |volume=1786 |issue=1 |doi=10.1063/1.4967594 |bibcode=2016AIPC.1786h0001A }}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |last1=Ketsdever |first1=Andrew |last2=Gimelshein |first2=Natalia |last3=Gimelshein |first3=Sergey |last4=Selden |first4=Nathaniel |title=Radiometric phenomena: From the 19th to the 21st century |journal=Vacuum |date=2012 |volume=86 |issue=11 |pages=1644–1662 |doi=10.1016/j.vacuum.2012.02.006 |bibcode=2012Vacuu..86.1644K }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Selden |first1=N. |last2=Ngalande |first2=C. |last3=Gimelshein |first3=S. |last4=Muntz |first4=E. === Low-density plasmas, materials processing and plasma processing ===

Considerable work has used DSMC and other rarefied gas dynamic approaches to understand and predict flows and behavior of low-density and weakly-ionized plasmas. In these cases, other simulation approaches are generally coupled with or overlaid on the DSMC to simulate the plasma interactions. This rich literature includes studies of ion sputtering and deposition,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Takekida |first1=Hideto |last2=Nanbu |first2=Kenichi |title=Particle modelling of inductively-coupled argon plasmas with wafer biasing |journal=Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics |date=2005 |volume=38 |issue=18 |pages=3461–3468 |doi=10.1088/0022-3727/38/18/022 |bibcode=2005JPhD...38.3461T }}</ref><ref>{{Cite report |title=A 2-D Self-Consistent DSMC Model for Chemically Reacting Low Pressure Plasma Reactors |last1=Bartel |first1=Timothy J. |last2=Economou |first2=Demetre |last3=Johannes |first3=Justine E. |date=1999-06-17 |publisher=Sandia National Labs., Albuquerque, NM (US); Sandia National Labs., Livermore, CA (US) |issue=SAND99–1532C |osti=7900 |oclc=68391759 }}</ref> chemical etching,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Nanbu |first1=K. |last2=Morimoto |first2=T. |last3=Suetani |first3=M. |date=1999 |title=Direct simulation Monte Carlo analysis of flows and etch rate in an inductively coupled plasma reactor |journal=IEEE Transactions on Plasma Science |volume=27 |issue=5 |pages=1379–1388 |doi=10.1109/27.799816 |bibcode=1999ITPS...27.1379N }}</ref> and chemical vapor deposition for materials processing.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rebrov |first1=A.K. |last2=Maltsev |first2=R.V. |last3=Safonov |first3=A.I. |last4=Timoshenko |first4=N.I. |title=Activated gas jet deposition |journal=Thin Solid Films |date=2011 |volume=519 |issue=14 |pages=4542–4544 |doi=10.1016/j.tsf.2011.01.290 |bibcode=2011TSF...519.4542R }}</ref> There is also extensive work on ion engines and Hall-effect thrusters.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bruno |first1=D. |last2=Capitelli |first2=M. |last3=Longo |first3=S. |last4=Minelli |first4=P. |last5=Taccogna |first5=F. |title=Particle kinetic modelling of rarefied gases and plasmas |journal=Plasma Sources Science and Technology |date=2003 |volume=12 |issue=4 |pages=S89–S97 |doi=10.1088/0963-0252/12/4/024 |bibcode=2003PSST...12S..89B }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Boyd |first1=Iain D. |title=Review of Hall Thruster Plume Modeling |journal=Journal of Spacecraft and Rockets |date=2001 |volume=38 |issue=3 |pages=381–387 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Tumuklu |first1=Ozgur |last2=Levin |first2=Deborah A. |title=Particle Simulations of the Effects of Atomic Oxygen on Ion Thruster Plumes |journal=Journal of === Need for hybrid methods ===

Some of above flows have vastly different density or Kn in some spatial or temporal regions where they transition between continuum and free-molecular conditions (plumes; hypersonic flows around complex shapes) and thus may require hybrid solution methods.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hash |first1=D. B. |last2=Hassan |first2=H. A. |title=Assessment of schemes for coupling Monte Carlo and Navier-Stokes solution methods |journal=Journal of Thermophysics and Heat Transfer |date=1996 |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=242–249 |doi=10.2514/3.781 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Schwartzentruber |first1=Thomas E. |last2=Scalabrin |first2=Leonardo C. |last3=Boyd |first3=Iain D. |title=Hybrid Particle-Continuum Simulations of Nonequilibrium Hypersonic Blunt-Body Flowfields |journal=Journal of Thermophysics and Heat Transfer |date=2008 |volume=22 |pages=29–37 |doi=10.2514/1.30216 |hdl=2027.42/77319 |hdl-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Fei |first1=Fei |last2=Jenny |first2=Patrick |title=A hybrid particle approach based on the unified stochastic particle Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook and DSMC methods |journal=Journal of Computational Physics |date=2021 |volume=424 |article-number=109858 |doi=10.1016/j.jcp.2020.109858 |bibcode=2021JCoPh.42409858F }}</ref>
